label: A Tour of Multiple View Geometry
notes: This opening chapter, printed pages 1 through 22, frames the entire book. It argues that multiple view geometry is not a bag of unrelated matrices but one projective language answering three questions: what survives imaging, what ambiguity matching leaves, and what assumptions upgrade a projective answer to a Euclidean one.

label: Why Projective Geometry
notes: Perspective projection turns a square into a quadrilateral and a circle into an ellipse, yet straight lines stay straight. The correct invariant is projective incidence, not Euclidean shape. Because a camera is itself a projective map, projective geometry is the natural language for both scene points and image measurements throughout the course.

label: Homogeneous Coordinates
notes: Homogeneous coordinates append a scale entry so that a point is a whole ray of nonzero vectors. Equality means agreement after normalization. A line is also a three vector, and a point lies on it exactly when their dot product vanishes, giving a clean symmetric incidence algebra for the plane.

label: Points and Lines at Infinity
notes: Setting the last coordinate to zero gives ideal points where parallel lines meet. They all sit on one line at infinity. Choosing that special line is what separates affine from projective structure, and its image under a homography is the visible horizon or vanishing line that the notebook constructs.

label: The Pinhole Camera
notes: A pinhole camera maps every point on a ray through the center to the same image coordinate, so depth is lost but incidence survives. The three by four camera matrix is a projective map of rank three from world points to image points, decomposing into intrinsic calibration, rotation, and translation.

label: Single View: Calibration and Vanishing Points
notes: From one image we can still recover structure. Vanishing points are images of directions, the points at infinity of parallel families. Their geometry constrains the calibration matrix through the image of the absolute conic, letting a single view yield angles, orientations, and partial metric information about the scene.

label: Two Views and the Fundamental Matrix
notes: With two separated centers a point in one image no longer fixes a point in the other; it fixes an epipolar line. The fundamental matrix packages this incidence: every correspondence satisfies x prime transpose F x equals zero, and F has rank two, encoding the entire two view relation independent of scene.

label: Epipolar Geometry Visualized
notes: Each epipolar line is the image of the ray back projected from the other view, and all such lines pass through the epipole, the image of the opposing camera center. This pencil of lines is the visual fingerprint of the fundamental matrix and reduces correspondence search from a plane to one line.

label: Reconstruction Ambiguity
notes: From uncalibrated images reconstruction is only projective. Replacing every point by H X and every camera by P H inverse leaves all image measurements unchanged, so a point cloud can be image perfect yet metrically distorted. Extra information narrows the ambiguity through the projective, affine, and metric strata.

label: The Euclidean Upgrade
notes: Calibration supplies the missing metric object. For intrinsics K the image of the absolute conic is omega equals K inverse transpose K inverse, and it lets images measure angles between back projected rays. Locating the plane at infinity removes affine ambiguity; fixing the absolute conic removes the remaining metric ambiguity.

label: Three and N Views
notes: Three views add the trifocal tensor, a richer incidence object relating points and lines across the triple and enabling transfer to a predicted third view. Across many images bundle adjustment jointly refines all cameras and structure by minimizing total reprojection error, the gold standard refinement of the whole pipeline.

label: The Reconstruction Pipeline
notes: The book is a dependency chain: projective representation, then camera projection, then correspondences giving two and three view constraints, then projective reconstruction upgraded by calibration to affine and metric structure. Dense stereo, surface models, and video augmentation are the rewards earned once that geometric chain is solved correctly.
